pulls.title: 8394260: x86: improve Adler32 intrinsic on AVX2
pulls.author: LangruiZhou
pulls.body_excerpt: ### Description The AVX2 loop in generate_updateBytesAdler32() processed 16 bytes per iteration using two vpshufb and four vpaddd instructions, and reduced the accumulators with vpmulld followed by a vphaddd chain. VPHADDD is not a cheap single-µop operation: it decodes to three µops on Intel P-cores — two in-lane shuffle µops plus one add — and those shuffle µops contend for the shuffle pipes; the AVX forms are also microcoded on AMD Zen and Intel E-cores ([uops.info](https://uops.info/html-instr/VPHADDD_YMM_YMM_YMM.html)). In a hot reduction loop this makes the vphaddd chain throughput-limit

pulls.title: 8393068: Optimize uniform vector byte shift operations using x86 GFNI instruction
pulls.author: jatin-bhateja
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi All, x86 AVX-512 targets provides packed shifts for 16, 32, and 64-bit lanes, but not for bytes. C2 lowers LShiftVB, RShiftVB, and URShiftVB by widening bytes to words, shifting, masking, and packing. That sequence is the byte-shift bottleneck. GFNI **gf2p8affineqb** instruction applies one 8×8 bit matrix to every byte. Logical left, logical right, and arithmetic right shifts by 0..7 are fixed matrices derived from the identity 0x0102040810204080. Patch uses this lowering for 128-, 256-, and 512-bit vectors when GFNI is available and keeps the existing widen/shift/pack path when GFNI is abs
